event.summary: Explicitly opening the agent host-add card preserves the intended approval test
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 9ff03ce91f191ea59f3ce16cefbd0b76d7fe599d. TLDR: Considered whether adding the explicit Open add dialog click removes coverage of an expected automatic opening or weakens protection against agent-triggered setup. It does not: automatic opening is forbidden, and the test still verifies no setup request occurs before Set up despite the saved skip preference, then verifies that origin survives the refused setup and reprobe. Source: provisioning.spec.ts:1442-1521; SPEC.md:4179-4195 (Agent-spawned sessions); SPEC_impl.md:9204-9217. Exact contract: 'The request never opens the dialog by itself, because the user did not start it'; 'An agent add always shows the setup confirmation when installation is needed, whatever the setup preference says, including after a refused setup submission is reopened.' SPEC.md, Keyboard focus / Opening and closing: 'A confirmation the user just opened starts on the action they asked for: focus starts on its enabled confirming button'. Suggested bucket: other (considered test regression, refuted). Confidence: confirmed by source and contract, no runtime observation. proposed_drop: explicit opening and focused Set up assertions follow the quoted contract; original suspected consequence was missing automatic-opening coverage. possible_cover: none known; coverage sources not searched. Could-be-highest: no, this candidate concerns the browser test only and its relevant permission assertions remain present. Caveat: this does not establish every production approval/focus path is correct.

event.summary: Short menu waits retain the per-host busy-state assertions
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462. TLDR: Considered whether the shorter menu timeout lets the regression test pass without showing each host's correct setup state. It does not: the retry encloses both opening the menu and asserting the required enabled/disabled Settings state, and no error is swallowed outside that retry. Source: provisioning.spec.ts:3741-3798 verifies both page rows running, both Settings disabled, then first completed/enabled and second still running/disabled; helpers/fleet.ts:1344-1401 passes options to menu toggle operations, panel visibility and measured-placement polling; :1443-1452 forwards the option from openHostMenu. Provisioning e2e backend action at crates/farhelm-helm/src/provisioning/e2e.rs:206-235 keeps an action held until released or its 30-second failure, supporting the documented reason for releasing retry attempts promptly. Suggested bucket: other (considered false-positive test regression, refuted). Confidence: confirmed by source, no runtime observation. proposed_drop: shortening a readiness wait changes when an attempt retries, not what must pass; an incorrect Settings state still cannot satisfy that attempt. possible_cover: none known; coverage sources not searched. Could-be-highest: no; this is browser-test observation behavior only. Caveats: timeout is per operation, not a one-second deadline for the entire helper; showHostsPanel keeps its ordinary readiness waits, but the caller has already opened that panel before the changing-menu observations. No claim of measured runtime reliability.

event.summary: Retirement test can replace its body assertion with a cleanup error
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. TLDR: When this browser regression test first fails a hard assertion and its cleanup also fails, the reported callback error can become an AggregateError about cleanup instead of the assertion that exposed the regression. This complicates diagnosis; assertion step/trace evidence remains, so the original assertion is not universally lost. Source checked: new retired-container-sessions.spec.ts:114-118 reads info.status !== info.expectedStatus inside the body's own finally and passes that value to cleanupOwnedSteps. Unchanged helpers/cleanup.ts:6-19 attempts each step, but only logs cleanup errors when bodyFailed is true; with false it throws AggregateError. e2e/package-lock.json:13-20,42-49,58-60 pins @playwright/test, playwright and playwright-core to 1.64.0. Caller-supplied already-recorded dependency source evidence establishes the timing premise for that locked runner: a hard expect records its failing step and rethrows before test status is changed; the runner awaits the complete callback, including finally, before its outer catch records body failure. Therefore a first hard assertion can leave info.status equal to expectedStatus in this finally; throwing cleanup AggregateError replaces the propagating assertion under JavaScript finally semantics. This timing differs from reading status in afterEach. Contract: the helper's own lines 3-4 promise 'An assertion failure remains the primary failure; cleanup errors accompany it in stderr.' The new caller does not reliably provide the argument needed for that contract. Capture body failure explicitly with catch/rethrow plus a local flag before finally, as appropriate for an in-body cleanup caller. Suggested bucket: other (test failure diagnostics, no product security/work-loss route). Confidence: confirmed source analysis using locally checked caller/helper/locked-version correspondence plus the expressly supplied runner-source premise; no runtime observation or reproduction. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: caller explicitly identifies existing mechanism cleanup-status-masks-body-assertion at other call sites and will extend it with this new in-range caller; no queue metadata read or searched. This is a linked caller finding, not a request for a second mechanism entry. Could-be-highest: no. Caveats: requires both a body hard assertion failure and cleanup rejection; helper still attempts later cleanup steps, and page-route separation/owned-id cleanup remain valid. This does not refute c4's narrow presentation/dispatch coverage or establish successful real Podman removal. Attribution: this test and its in-body status argument are introduced by the assigned commit, even though the helper already existed. No universal cleanup success or primary-error preservation is claimed.
